name: e05_crises_regimes
title: 5. Crisis alpha or crisis lag? Stress periods, regimes and convexity
text:
**Question.** Does EMA50/200 earn the "crisis alpha" trend following is sold on, and what does it pay for it when crashes are fast?

**Setup.** EMA50/200 vs buy & hold on SPY (from 1994-11-28), QQQ and BTC-USD, next-close fills, default costs. Crisis windows are peak to trough (`universe.CRISES`, plus the 2018 and 2021-22 crypto crashes for BTC); because a rule that exits near the low looks fine inside the window, each crisis is also measured from the peak until buy & hold regained its pre-crisis level (or the next crisis began). Regime labels (SPY vs SMA200, VIX terciles, SPY drawdown) are known at the prior close.

**Findings.**
- **Only 2 of 4 SPY episodes longer than six months paid.** SPY Dot-com bust -5% vs -48% (+47.3 pp to recovery); GFC -11% vs -55% (+30.4 pp to Apr 2011, when the next crisis began). Episodes longer than six months (all assets) averaged +22.9 pp in the window and +16.6 pp to recovery; shorter ones +1.1 pp and -13.5 pp.
- **Fast crashes cost.** SPY to recovery: 2011 euro/downgrade -12.0 pp (missed 16%); Q4 2018 selloff -8.9 pp (missed 19%); COVID crash -28.8 pp (missed 44%); 2025 tariff shock -11.2 pp. In COVID its first day in cash was the trough day itself, and it was back in 55 bars after the low; in 2025 it held through the low and sold into the rebound.
- **In-window numbers flatter the rule.** SPY 2022: +11.7 pp in the window, -0.2 pp to recovery (re-entry 84 bars after the low). Over all 19 episodes it helped (> +2 pp) in 5 (SPY Dot-com bust, SPY GFC, QQQ GFC, QQQ 2022 inflation bear, BTC-USD 2021-22 crypto crash) and hurt (< −2 pp) in 11.
- **Regimes.** Below SPY's SMA200 (close to the rule's own signal) exposure was 25%, yet buy & hold still earned 8.7% a year there (Sharpe 0.36 vs 0.28 for the rule): below-trend days include the sharpest rebounds. In the top VIX tercile exposure was 59%, earning 12.1% a year vs 16.5% at 18.0% vs 26.8% vol. Full sample: Sharpe 0.59 vs 0.53, max drawdown -36.3% vs -55.2%.
- **No smile on SPY.** Monthly capture 76% up / 66% down; quarterly c = -0.35 (t = -0.88); QQQ +0.88 (t = +3.92); BTC-USD +0.16 (t = +2.96).
- **Concentrated payoff.** The trailing 3-year Sharpe led buy & hold in 36% of windows and trailed in 53% (median -0.08); 77% of the leading windows contain the Dot-com bust and GFC, so the higher full-sample Sharpe rests on those episodes.

**Interpretation.** A moving-average crossover is a low-pass filter, so it lags by construction (Levine & Pedersen 2016). The lag is harmless in long, deep bears (Dot-com bust, GFC) that give it months to step aside. It is costly in V-shaped shocks (2011 euro/downgrade, Q4 2018 selloff, COVID crash, 2025 tariff shock), where the exit comes near (or after) the low and the re-entry after the rebound, and in shallow corrections (2015-16 China/oil) too small to pay for the round trip. The crisis alpha and straddle-like payoff of Fung & Hsieh (2001) and Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen (2017) belong to diversified long-short futures books; a long-or-cash rule cannot profit from a crash and gives up rebound quarters (SPY shows no significant curvature; QQQ and BTC-USD show a smile, earned in deep bear quarters spent in cash; plain OLS t-statistics, so indicative only). Its value hinges on the sample containing a slow, deep bear.
after: Protection compounds returns strictly inside each peak-to-trough window; the peak-to-recovery edge extends the window until buy & hold regains its starting level, so it charges the rule for the rebound it missed; it is cut at the start of the next listed crisis so no period is counted twice (SPY GFC stops at April 2011; BTC-USD 2018 crypto winter stops at February 2020). Long uncapped cycles (SPY 2000-06) still include unrelated whipsaws after the crisis. QQQ's dot-com bust is not covered: after the EMA200 warm-up its backtest starts in 2001. Quarterly convexity t-statistics are plain OLS and only indicative. The crisis list and the two crypto windows are dated peak to trough with hindsight, which is fine for attribution but would be look-ahead in a trading rule.
